policy: Course coordinates are independently digitized from licensed georeferenced aerial imagery. Pinned raster and source hashes reproduce each draft centerline. Timing GPS remains private.

records.evidence: The full paved circuit follows the main straight, northern hairpin, upper switchback and southern wooded technical section visible in the independent 2019 aerial image. Pit-entry and paddock driveways are excluded. The operator identifies one full circuit with 18 turns; its advertised 2.2-mile length is approximate and is not used to scale the geometry.

The association lists Kinsmen Kart Club at Dixon. The independently visible paved full circuit retains the northeastern bulb, central hairpin and two western hairpins. The small diagonal infield connector, pit access and neighboring dirt speedway are excluded. Fine corner alignment and driving direction remain draft.

The operator's Kart #1 course uses both west and east kart loops: Long Beach, The Glen, Zolder, Daytona, Imola, Monza, the Mulsanne Straight and Monte Carlo triangular return via Spa. The independently visible paved centerline retains those branches and excludes the oval shortcut, hot pits and surrounding main road circuit. Operator route dimensions identify a full course of roughly 952 m; mapping is not scaled to that distance.

The narrow two-straight test loop east of the TRC Ohio high-speed oval is independently digitized from public-domain 2023 aerial imagery. The operator identifies the Ohio proving-ground site and its testing facilities; the catalogue name and timing location identify this specific loop. The small southern turnaround and northern crossing return are retained; the large high-speed oval and adjacent handling roads are excluded. Turnaround alignment and direction remain draft.

records.referenceId: United States/Thermal Club Twin Palms Short
records.evidence: Twin Palms Short retains the middle Desert course with its northern undulations and eastern roundabout return, joined to the South Palm outer course. It excludes the North Palm extension, the South Palm inner technical loop, karting roads and pit access. Independently read public-domain 2022 NAIP pavement centers identify the full short branch sequence; route distance is unscaled and historical barriers and direction remain draft. The 2022 aerial centerline differs from the 3999 m catalogue scalar; the geometry is not scaled to match it.

The operator’s Rallycross configuration retains the northern and western gravel arc, the long central asphalt hairpin and the southern outer gravel return. The inner karting loops, the asphalt-only outer course and pit lane are excluded. The route is manually digitized on the independently georeferenced GUGiK orthoimage. Surface transitions, temporary barriers, fine corner alignment and historical configuration remain provisional. No diagram coordinates or comparison-course GPS are used.

The operator identifies the Autodrom Jastrzab training and motorsport complex. This configuration uses both Northern hairpins, the long Western return and its small infield hairpin, the central triangular-island return and Eastern S bends. The Southern connection crosses the paved training apron and bypasses the separate Southern skid circle. The route is independently digitized from freely reusable GUGiK government orthoimagery because the public map omits the Northern return and several source ways contain angular shortcuts. All pixel anchors are picked on visible pavement in the government raster; neither catalogue picture vertices nor timing GPS set course coordinates. The independently measured 1741.0 m versus the catalogue 1715 m is retained, with a 45 m allowance for provisional centerline and historical temporary-cone alignment. Direction, temporary barriers and corner alignment remain draft.

The operator identifies Track 3 as the wet handling course with a 0.45-mile short configuration. This catalogue branch retains the Northern turn-in, middle S, rounded Southern return and Eastern hairpin of that short wet loop. The surrounding dry handling road and outer wet-loop extension are excluded. The centerline is manually digitized only on visible pavement in pinned public-domain 2023 USGS/USDA NAIP imagery. The independent 663.6 m measured route remains unscaled against the 698 m catalogue scalar and the approximate advertised 0.45-mile length; a 45 m catalogue allowance retains historical corner and surface-path differences as a draft limitation. No catalogue image vertices or timing positions determine these coordinates.

The open hillclimb follows the paved Western first corner past Goodwood House, the Northeast straight, Molecomb left turn and Northern wooded return. The operator course plan identifies this sequence; unrelated Eastern estate roads and grass paths are excluded. Centerline vertices are independently inspected on 2014 Environment Agency georeferenced imagery; the wooded Northern section is corroborated by pinned public road mapping. Tree cover, historic timing extent and fine corner alignment remain draft. The timing catalogue scalar is 2806 m while the operator describes a 1.16-mile hillclimb; the independent timed route is not scaled to either figure. Identification plan: https://www.goodwood.com/globalassets/pdfs/motorsport/fos/fos-3dmap-nocf-2025.pdf . The independent gate-to-gate route measures 1679.8 m, 1126.2 m shorter than the catalogue scalar and approximately 187 m shorter than the operator description. This unresolved historical timing-extent discrepancy is retained with an explicit 1150 m allowance, rather than adding unrelated roads or extending the route beyond its timing endpoints.

The historical Configuration H uses the Northern full terminal loop, Western upper S return, central small hairpin and Eastern middle straight, with the Southern internal chicane before the Southwestern terminal return. The 2006 organizer report identifies Configuration H, avoiding the rough old back sector. The original operator course plan identifies the alternate internal branches: https://www.kstreetstudio.com/files/tinyvette/renofernley/RF-TrackMap.pdf . Centerline pixels are independently inspected on public-domain 2022 NAIP imagery; no comparison-diagram pixels or coordinates supply geometry. The larger Western back sector, large central U and pit/staging lanes are excluded. Fine historical barrier, surface and Southern chicane alignment remain draft; the independent measured length is unscaled.

The identified historical E course retains the Western long narrow return, upper Western short loop, inner middle S, Southern linking bend and complete Eastern middle straight. The original operator roadcourse plan establishes the old-sector and alternate Southern connections. The Northeastern full loop, upper Northern S and Southwestern terminal loop are excluded. All course pixels are independently inspected pavement centerline anchors on public-domain 2022 NAIP imagery; comparison diagrams supply branch identity only. Fine corner, old timing extent, degraded pavement and temporary barrier alignment remain draft, without scaling to the catalogue distance.

The operator identifies the 1.9-mile Western course. Its published plan includes the Western Northern turnaround, central diagonal and inner Southern hairpin, Northern carousel, short Northeastern return and Eastern closing straight. These branches follow the independently inspected graded road alignment in public-domain July 2022 NAIP imagery. The operator construction history dates this period before final paving. The trace is a historical construction-alignment draft; finished pavement centerline, temporary barriers and fine corner alignment are unverified. It excludes the separate Eastern circuit, paddock and access roads. No operator or comparison diagram pixels supply course coordinates, and no coordinates are scaled to a nominal distance.

GeoSN historical orthophoto capture year 2012 identifies paved centerlines independently. The manufacturer identifies separately usable 3.7 km and 2.2 km courses and configurable training sections. The comparison shapes show alternatives, so named branch paths preserve each configuration set rather than asserting one timed lap. Later dynamic-course additions are excluded. Historical direction, lap choice and present-day corner alignment remain unverified.

The newer southern extension, kart course, dragway and pit road are excluded. Coordinates come from independent public georeferencing, without fitting the supplied diagram or scalar. Historical direction and fine corner alignment remain draft.

Source direction and fine centerline alignment remain draft.

Historical branch choice, direction and fine centerline alignment remain draft. Coordinates are not fitted to a private diagram or scalar distance.

This network measures unique branches rather than one timed lap; historical direction and fine alignment remain draft.

Southern loop with its western outer bend, inner return and full eastern straight. The operator identifies the 4.1 km Southern Loop; the full course plan separates paddock, karting and energy-road access, all excluded. Native satellite ground resolution is 10 m. Nearest-neighbor rendering does not add resolution. Fine corner alignment and historical direction remain draft; no vertices are fitted to private diagrams, timing positions or nominal distance.

Historical winter motorsport oval on the Ramenskoe hippodrome. The hippodrome operator documents annual winter car races from 1997 to 2011. The municipal report identifies the 1,600 m ice oval and 16 m width. Independent 2025 satellite imagery supplies the permanent oval footprint; temporary snow/ice racing-line alignment is unverified and remains a draft. The unrelated northern sports track and inner field are excluded. Native satellite ground resolution is 10 m. Nearest-neighbor rendering does not add resolution. Fine corner alignment and historical direction remain draft; no vertices are fitted to private diagrams, timing positions or nominal distance.

The organizer 2026 programme, pages 8 and 9, identifies the full road racing route: Avenue Gilles-Villeneuve, pool return, Boulevard du Carmel, Rue de Calonne and Rue Papineau with the Ryan hairpin. Pavement and painted race curbs are independently digitized from the licensed 2019 Quebec orthophoto. The oval, rallycross course, parking roads and pit lane are excluded. Historical road alignment and the western carriageway of Boulevard du Carmel are retained; current street widening is not substituted. The independently measured centerline is approximately 2.374 km versus the supplied 2.437 km nominal value; the difference is retained rather than scaling the course. The source image has 20 cm native resolution but this bounded WMS render samples approximately 0.78 m on the ground. Fine corner alignment and direction remain draft. No vertices are fitted to private diagrams, timing coordinates or nominal length.

The municipal newspaper reports the February 2013 Russian winter-track championship at Samara-Ring in Kurumoch. The complete oval footprint is independently digitized from the June 15, 2013 Landsat 8 panchromatic scene, before subsequent site redevelopment. Field roads, access roads and the oval infield are excluded. The 15 m native ground resolution, exact UTM transform, source DN clip, rendering stretch, scene identity and hashes are pinned. Nearest-neighbor rendering does not add resolution. The oval centerline is a historical draft; winter snow barriers, precise racing-line placement and direction remain unverified. No vertices are fitted to private diagrams, timing positions or nominal distance.

The Incheon Institute government research report identifies the Sadong block 90 Ansan racing course, its 2.871 km design and approximately 700 m main straight, and describes the unfinished 2005 construction and later partial dismantling. The complete surviving pavement footprint, including the western main straight, northern chicane, eastern loop and inner triangular return, is independently digitized from the October 5, 2014 Landsat 8 panchromatic scene. The neighboring river roads, southern roundabout, parking roads and pit lane are excluded. The 15 m native ground resolution, exact UTM transform, source DN clip, rendering stretch, scene identity and hashes are pinned. Nearest-neighbor rendering does not add resolution. The independently digitized surviving course measures approximately 3.540 km, which conflicts with both the supplied 2.868 km scalar and the report design length. This discrepancy is retained as a review issue; the geometry is not scaled or shortened to fit a distance. This is a historical pavement draft. Temporary barriers, fine chicane alignment and direction remain unverified. No vertices are fitted to private diagrams, timing positions or nominal distance.
